name: smooth_shift_dirty_parity
description: Smooth shift outward, inward, and on a single face of a multi-face base, over non-planar / poled / reflex / degenerate geometry. The existing smooth-shift fixture is a capture on a stock cube; these are the cells a cube cannot express.

provenance.notes: The direction a shifted face travels is an averaged normal, and on a non-planar ring or a pole there is more than one defensible average -- so agreement here is a real constraint, not a restatement of the obvious. CHANNELS: the sweep's comparison was never vertex-only -- it compared the vertex multiset, the edge multiset, faces BOTH as ordered rings (winding shows) and as unordered position sets, the material partition, the per-face 'did this face's own tag change', and the post-command selection. Re-checked independently over all 215 frozen cases: ZERO agree on vertices while differing on ordered face rings, so nothing frozen here is a vertex-channel-only agreement. PRECISION: the sweep compared at 1e-4 and this fixture's tolerance matches it. The actual reproduction is far tighter -- 208 of the 215 cases are bit-identical at the dumps' 6 decimals and the remaining 7 agree to 3e-6 or better, that being the worst deviation anywhere in the set. The tolerance is the MEASUREMENT's bound, not the data's.
